---
title: File uploads
callout-appearance: simple
---

[`content_pdf_file()`](../reference/content_pdf_file.qmd) and [`content_image_file()`](../reference/content_image_file.qmd) re-send the file's bytes on every turn. For large files, or files you want to reference repeatedly, upload the file to the provider once and reference it by id instead — the bytes are sent a single time, and every later turn just points at the reference.

Use [`chat.files`](../reference/Chat.qmd#files) to upload, list, fetch metadata for, download, and delete provider-hosted files.

```python
import chatlas as ctl

chat = ctl.ChatOpenAI()
uploaded = chat.files.upload("quarterly-report.pdf")
chat.chat(uploaded, "Summarize the key findings.")
```

`upload()` returns a [`ContentUploaded`](../reference/types.ContentUploaded.qmd), a reference (id, mime type, provider) rather than the file's content. Pass it to `.chat()` just like any other content object, and reuse it across as many turns as you like:

```python
chat.chat(uploaded, "Now list the risks mentioned.")
```

## Managing uploaded files

```python
chat.files.list()          # -> list[FileMetadata]
meta = chat.files.get(uploaded.id)
chat.files.delete(uploaded.id)
```

Each of these has an `_async` counterpart (`upload_async()`, `list_async()`, `get_async()`, `download_async()`, `delete_async()`) for use with [async chats](async.qmd).

[`FileMetadata`](../reference/types.FileMetadata.qmd) normalizes fields across providers (`id`, `filename`, `mime_type`, `size_bytes`, `created_at`, `expires_at`, `provider`, plus provider-native fields in `extra`).

::: callout-warning
### You can't download what you uploaded

Providers gate downloads on how a file was created, and none of them allow it for files sent via `chat.files.upload()` — expect a provider error there. OpenAI refuses `purpose="user_data"` (what `upload()` uses) while allowing `purpose="batch"`/`"batch_output"`, so the input and result files behind [`batch_chat()`](../reference/batch_chat.qmd) *are* downloadable. Anthropic marks uploaded files non-downloadable, and Google only serves bytes back for model-generated files (e.g. Gemini video output).
:::

## Supported providers

File management works with `ChatOpenAI()` (the Responses API), `ChatAnthropic()`, and `ChatGoogle()` (the Gemini Developer API). Everything else — `ChatOpenAICompletions()`, OpenAI-compatible third parties (`ChatGroq()`, `ChatMistral()`, `ChatOllama()`, etc.), `ChatAzureOpenAI()`, `ChatBedrockAnthropic()`, `ChatPosit()` (its Anthropic flavor proxies through a gateway that doesn't support the beta Files API), and Vertex-backed chats (`ChatVertex()`, or `ChatGoogle()` configured for Vertex) — raises `NotImplementedError` from `chat.files.*`.

::: callout-note
### Anthropic: beta API

Anthropic's Files API is still in beta. chatlas automatically adds the required `anthropic-beta: files-api-2025-04-14` header whenever a turn references an uploaded file — there's nothing you need to configure.
:::

::: callout-note
### Google: 48-hour expiry, no Vertex support

Files uploaded to the Gemini Developer API automatically expire after 48 hours. The Files API isn't available on Vertex AI at all, so `chat.files.upload()` raises `NotImplementedError` on a Vertex-backed chat. To reference a file you've already put in Cloud Storage, construct the reference by hand instead:

```python
import chatlas as ctl

chat = ctl.ChatVertex()
gcs_file = ctl.types.ContentUploaded(
    id="gs://my-bucket/report.pdf",
    mime_type="application/pdf",
    provider="google",
)
chat.chat(gcs_file, "Summarize this.")
```
:::

::: callout-note
### Google: large media uploads block until ready

Gemini processes large media (video, audio, multi-GB uploads) asynchronously, and refuses to use a file that isn't yet `ACTIVE`. So for Google, `upload()` waits for processing to finish before returning — meaning it can block for a while on a big video, and raises if the file fails to process. The reference you get back is always ready to use.
:::

::: callout-note
### OpenAI Chat Completions: no uploaded images

`ChatOpenAICompletions()` can reference an uploaded PDF or text document, but not an uploaded image — the Chat Completions API doesn't support it. Use `ChatOpenAI()` (Responses API) for uploaded images, or pass the image inline with `content_image_file()`.
:::
